hypotheses.justification: This follows from the other hypotheses. Mathlib's `RootPairing.instFlipIsReduced [P.IsReduced] [IsTorsionFree R N] : P.flip.IsReduced` (Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/RootSystem/Reduced.lean) also needs `[Finite ι] [CharZero R] [IsDomain R] [Module.IsTorsionFree R M]`. The theorem already has the first three. Torsion-freeness is automatic for a root pairing over a domain: `RootPairing` carries `isPerfPair_toLinearMap`, so `P.toLinearMap : M → (N →ₗ[R] R)` is injective (`LinearMap.IsPerfPair.bijective_left`). `R` is torsion-free over itself (instance in Torsion/Free.lean), and `N →ₗ[R] R` is torsion-free by the instance in Algebra/Module/LinearMap/Basic.lean. `Function.Injective.moduleIsTorsionFree` (with `map_smul`) then gives `IsTorsionFree R M`; the same argument with `P.flip` (perfect pairing `P.toLinearMap.flip`) gives `IsTorsionFree R N`. The modified proof builds these two instances and `P.flip.IsReduced` with `have`, then runs the existing proof unchanged. It cannot be deleted together with `[P.IsReduced]`: each one can be deleted only while the other stays.

Symmetric to the other entry. `P.flip.flip = P` holds by `rfl` (`RootPairing.flip_flip`), so `instFlipIsReduced` applied to `P.flip` (using `[P.flip.IsReduced]`, `[Finite ι] [CharZero R] [IsDomain R]`, and torsion-freeness of `N` and `M`) yields `P.flip.flip.IsReduced`, which is `P.IsReduced`. The torsion-freeness instances come from the perfect pairing over the domain `R`, as described in the other entry (`IsPerfPair.bijective_left`/`bijective_right`, the `LinearMap` torsion-free instance, and `Function.Injective.moduleIsTorsionFree`). The proof adds a `have` for `P.IsReduced` and is otherwise unchanged. Only one of `[P.IsReduced]` and `[P.flip.IsReduced]` can be deleted, not both.
